body: Thanks for reporting this issue! Your suspicion is indeed correct. Every invocation is wrapped and submitted to the `ForkJoinPool` which does not limit the queue size or block in any way. I‘ll take a closer look in the next few days.

I pushed 4831d24 to master that solved the issue for me locally.

@jarnbjo Before closing this issue, could you please test with the latest 5.3.0-SNAPSHOT from [Sonatype's snapshot repository](https://oss.sonatype.org/content/repositories/snapshots/) in your project?
@marcphilipp I appreciate the very quick fix! I hope that I have time tomorrow to take a look at it, but if not, I'm away for two weeks and won't be able to verify the fix until I'm back.
Thanks for testing and providing an updated sample. I'll dig deeper in the next few days.

I finally got around to looking into this issue again and increased the queue size limit in 95fbba8.

@jarnbjo Could you please give it another try?

Sure, it seems to work much better now.

Just a question out of curiosity: Currently, the implementation seems to use forEach on the argument source stream, create some kind of test context around it and from there, a ForkJoinTask which is submitted to a ForkJoinPool. Wouldn't it be much easier to use a ThreadPoolExecutor, which is fed by a work queue directly backed by the argument stream?

> Just a question out of curiosity: Currently, the implementation seems to use forEach on the argument source stream, create some kind of test context around it and from there, a ForkJoinTask which is submitted to a ForkJoinPool. Wouldn't it be much easier to use a ThreadPoolExecutor, which is fed by a work queue directly backed by the argument stream?

For this simple use case that would work. However, generally speaking, a `TestDescriptor` could spawn additional dynamic children which would have to be executed before finishing the enclosing test descriptor and so on.

> Sure, it seems to work much better now.
